newsitem.title: USA: U.S. supports French action in Central Africa.
newsitem.headline: U.S. supports French action in Central Africa.

text.p: The United States said on Monday it fully supported France in launching reprisal raids at the weekend against army mutineers in the Central African Republican after two French officers were killed.

"We understand that the French government acted as it should have acted in its own defence and in defence of the duly-constituted government of the Central African Republic," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
"The United States fully supports the response of the French military because its soldiers were attacked," Burns told a news briefing.
This is the third army mutiny in less than a year in the Central African Republic, a former French colony where French troops are stationed under a defence pact.
France accused mutineers of gunning down the two unarmed officers on Saturday and said Sunday's raids were in self-defence.
Burns said the United States hoped for a speedy end to the rebellion and a return to "civility and the rule of law".
He said all 34 U.S. citizens in the Central African Republic were safe and accounted for.
The U.S. embassy in the capital Bangui has advised Americans not to leave their homes while the disturbances continue.
